articles.title: Several Vehicles Set on Fire Under Bacup Arches on Rochdale Road
articles.excerpt: Several vehicles caught fire under the Bacup Arches on Rochdale Road early this morning, with loud explosions reported as the incident unfolded.
articles.content_html:
Several vehicles were on fire under the Bacup Arches on Rochdale Road overnight. The incident occurred at around 2am, with loud explosions reported as the cars went up in flames.

Emergency services responded to the scene, and the fire was extinguished shortly after. No injuries have been reported in connection with the incident.

The cause of the fire is currently unknown, and investigations are ongoing. Local residents reported hearing the explosions and seeing the flames from nearby streets.

Authorities are urging anyone with information about the incident to come forward.

articles.title: Roadworks on Princess Street to Begin on 7 September 2026
articles.excerpt: Queen Street in Rochdale will be closed for roadworks from 7 September to 17 September 2026, affecting traffic flow in the area.
articles.content_html:
A section of Queen Street will be temporarily closed for roadworks from 12 midnight on Monday, 7 September 2026, until 11.59pm on Thursday, 17 September 2026.

The closure will affect the stretch of Queen Street between the junctions with Whitehall Street and Duke Street. During this period, no waiting will be allowed in this area.

Motorists are advised to plan their journeys accordingly, as the roadworks may impact traffic flow.

For more information, residents can view a map of roadworks across Greater Manchester on the Rochdale Borough Council website.

articles.title: Two men injured in Heywood crash on Moss Hall Road
articles.excerpt: Two men were taken to hospital with serious injuries following a crash involving two cars on Moss Hall Road in Heywood.
articles.content_html:
A crash involving two cars occurred on Moss Hall Road in Heywood at around 7.45am on Tuesday, July 28. Two men, aged 35 and 44, were taken to hospital with serious injuries, according to a spokesperson for Greater Manchester Police.

Emergency services, including police and paramedics, responded to the incident. An air ambulance reportedly landed nearby as part of the response. Residents noted that a section of the road was closed for several hours following the crash.

Officers from Greater Manchester Police's Serious Collision Investigation Unit are investigating the incident. They are seeking any witnesses or individuals with relevant footage from the area, including CCTV, dashcam, or mobile phone recordings.

Anyone with information is encouraged to contact police on 0161 856 4741 or via the Live Chat service, quoting log 616 of 28/07/26. Alternatively, information can be provided anonymously to Crimestoppers at 0800 555 111.

articles.title: Roadworks on Birtle Road in Heywood to Begin on 24 August 2026
articles.excerpt: Birtle Road in Heywood will undergo roadworks from 24 to 28 August 2026, resulting in a temporary closure affecting traffic flow.
articles.content_html:
Birtle Road in Heywood will be temporarily closed for roadworks from Monday, 24 August 2026, to Friday, 28 August 2026. The closure will take place daily from 10am to 4pm.

The affected section of Birtle Road will be closed starting at the junction with Gristlehurst Lane and extending 95 metres southward. Due to the nature of the closure, there will be no alternative route for vehicles.

Motorists are advised to plan their journeys accordingly, as the closure may impact traffic flow during the specified hours.

For further details, residents can view a map of roadworks across Greater Manchester on the Rochdale Borough Council website.

articles.title: Hopwood Triangle Traffic Trial to Continue Pending Township Vote
articles.excerpt: The Hopwood Triangle traffic calming trial will remain in place until a formal vote by the Heywood Township, following widespread criticism from residents and motorists.
articles.content_html:
A traffic calming trial at the Hopwood Triangle in Heywood will continue pending a formal vote by the Heywood Township. Rochdale Council announced that the scheme, which has faced significant criticism since its introduction, cannot be removed until the township holds a meeting to vote on its future.

The trial introduced several changes to the roads around the Hopwood Triangle, including the closure of Middleton Road at its junction with Manchester Road near St John's Church. This measure was implemented to prevent drivers from using the route as a shortcut. Additionally, Magdala Street has been made one way towards Manchester Road, and new parking restrictions for heavy goods vehicles (HGVs) along with a 20mph speed limit have been established on surrounding residential roads.

North Heywood councillor Bev Place expressed her disappointment that the trial could not be ended immediately, as she had hoped. She stated that highways officers informed her of the need for a township meeting to formally vote on the matter. Councillor Place is working to arrange an extraordinary meeting, as the next scheduled meeting is not until 22nd September. She encouraged residents to share their views directly with Rochdale Council's highways team, noting that she has received numerous objections that must be submitted via email to be formally considered.

A spokesperson for Rochdale Council confirmed that there is no set date for the removal of the traffic restrictions and that they are in discussions with contractors regarding the timeline. The council also mentioned that traffic modelling is not typically conducted for residential side street schemes, and that a live trial is deemed the most effective method for assessing the impact on traffic levels and road safety.
